I had made a reservation, but it looked like there was plenty of space for walk ins as well. This was also my first time trying ramen in India after having it across several Southeast Asian countries, so I was quite curious to see how it compared.

I ordered the Signature Chicken Ramen (₹800+) and the Prawn Sushi (₹800+). The sushi was easily the highlight of the meal, fresh, well balanced, and something I would happily order again. The ramen, however, was a mixed experience. The broth initially reminded me more of a local chicken curry than the rich, comforting flavour I usually associate with ramen. Interestingly, the taste did grow on me as I continued eating, but it still fell short of my expectations overall. A nice little touch I appreciated was that each plate comes with a motivational quote printed on it, adding a bit of personality to the dining experience.

The restaurant is located on the first floor of Rex Walk. There is some construction happening near the lift exit, and I was surprised there weren’t any direction signs to guide customers to the restaurant. The staff’s enthusiastic Japanese greetings can also feel a bit overwhelming at first, almost as loud and energetic as a busy Shivajinagar market. Once you get past that, though, the restaurant has a pleasant atmosphere.

They also offer a vegetarian ramen option, and the restaurant is wheelchair friendly, which is always good to see. While the ramen wasn’t quite what I had hoped for, the sushi, comfortable setting, and thoughtful little details made it a worthwhile visit. The atmosphere feels lively yet intimate — perfect for date nights, casual hangouts, or even solo ramen cravings. Watching the chefs prepare fresh ramen and skewers right in front of you adds a unique charm to the experience. The mango beer was refreshing, fruity, and paired beautifully with the rich, flavorful ramen.

We also ordered the Garlic Mayo Yaki and Teriyaki Mayo, and both were packed with flavor — especially if you enjoy that indulgent mayo-based Japanese twist. Nothing felt average; each dish had its own standout taste and was well-executed.

We trusted our chef's recommendations, and it paid off beautifully. The salmon sashimi — served over crushed ice with signature spicing — was a revelation in simplicity: silky, pristine, and elevated just enough without overpowering the freshness of the fish. blocks.summary: True Yudofu is a Kyoto temple specialty, so it's rare in Bengaluru — but EBISU is the standout here with a confirmed tofu dish (agadashi tofu, hot broth poured over silken tofu), the closest you'll get to that Zen ritual. The others are top-rated Japanese spots worth asking about tofu preparations.
